items.title: For a good triple a locally bounded complex of finite locally free modules representing the twist exists whenever one exists for the original
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness)

items.difficulty_reason: Letting X, D, I, M be as in Situation labelled situation-complex-and-divisor with (X, D, M) a good triple, the lemma says that if M is represented by a locally bounded complex M^bullet of finite locally free O_X-modules, then L eta_I M is represented by a locally bounded complex Q^bullet of finite locally free O_{X'}-modules (statement lines 13534-13544). The proof takes Q^bullet = eta_I M^bullet, which represents L eta_I M by Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-Leta, and reduces the boundedness and local freeness checks to the affine local case, where boundedness is clear (proof lines 13546-13552). It then chooses an affine chart (U, A, f, M^bullet) for (X, D, M) with the ideals I_i(M^bullet, f) principal and with each M^i|_U finite free, which is possible because the triple is good, and writes N^i = Gamma(U, M^i|_U) to obtain a bounded complex N^bullet of finite free A-modules representing the same object of D(A) as M^bullet by Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-affine-compare-bounded (proof lines 13554-13562). Since I_i(N^bullet, f) is principal for all i by More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-ideal-well-defined, the complex eta_f N^bullet is bounded with finite locally free terms, and because Q^i|_U corresponds to eta_f N^i by Lemma labelled lemma-eta-stalks the conclusion follows (proof lines 13564-13567). Passing from an arbitrary locally free representative to a finite free complex on a good affine chart, so that the principal-ideal hypothesis makes eta_f preserve finite locally freeness, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
